newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Ahold sees major Q1 profit rise.
newsitem.headline: Ahold sees major Q1 profit rise.

text.p: Dutch supermarkets group Koninklijke Ahold NV said on Tuesday its turnover had surged by 48.2 percent to 14.0 billion guilders in the first quarter of 1997 and predicted major profit growth.

"For the first quarter of 1997, Ahold expects a substantial rise of operating profits. The profit after tax will be considerably higher (than in the year-ago period)," the company said in a statement.
Ahold reiterated its forecast that 1997 full-year net earnings would be considerably higher than 1996's and that earnings per share would grow significantly.
In 1996, the group posted a full-year net profit of 632.4 million guilders or 4.30 guilders per share.

Ahold said its hefty turnover rise in the first quarter of the current year reflected last year's takeover of U.S. retailer Stop&Shop. Excluding the effect of this acquisition, first quarter sales grew by 17.1 percent.
Currency rate changes had a positive effect on first quarter sales of 9.8 percent.
Ahold's first quarter sales in the Netherlands grew by 6.1 percent to 4.7 billion guilders and turnover in the rest of Europe went up by 32.1 percent to 693 million guilders.
In the U.S., first quarter sales showed a year-on-year growth of 53.9 percent to $4.2 billion.
Sales in Brazil totalled 474 million guilders and in the Asia Pacific region 274 million guilders, the company said.
Ahold will publish its figures for the first quarter of 1997 on June 12.
